elements.element: Vendor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: IBM must maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: IBM must maintain commercial general liability insurance of USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: IBM must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor shall maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires USD 5,000,000 of cyber and privacy liability insurance where IBM hosts, stores, or otherwise processes Customer Components or other Customer data.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: IBM must maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance upon request.
elements.evidence: IBM must provide certificates evidencing the required coverage upon Customer's request.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The required USD 2,000,000 professional liability limit exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor shall maintain cyber liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires USD 5,000,000 of cyber and privacy liability insurance where IBM hosts, stores, or otherwise processes Customer Components or other Customer data, exceeding the USD 2,000,000 fallback.

result.reason: The operative language meets every preferred requirement and therefore also exceeds both fallback limits. It preserves the existing risk-of-loss provisions without contradiction. It is not minimal because it additionally requires all coverages to continue for one year after termination, a duration not included in either stated position and potentially ill-suited to workers' compensation and occurrence-based CGL coverage.
